rules.sentence: Mucocutaneous bleeding, coupled with large platelets and thrombocytopenia, points towards a platelet disorder.
BSS should always be considered in the differential of a persistent or refractory ITP.[30]
A reevaluation with aggregation studies (especially ristocetin) and flow cytometry will be needed to confirm the diagnosis of BSS.
Large platelets or thrombocytopenia on peripheral smear review is NOT a feature of hemophilia.
